text: Outside, hundreds of people are glued to their phones. One point two million just watched Mok try to kill Jaeha.
Inside, two minutes left. Lyra would gladly leave the men who tried to murder him. Jaeha's rule has no exceptions.
So everyone climbs: Borro, with five fresh minutes, hauling two unconscious hunters and Jaeha, and Mok with Nib's knife right below him.
Then a flooded passage, walls cracking, the light at the end shrinking. Nine seconds.
They burst into the sunlight, and everyone comes back: Borro carrying two hunters, Lyra herding four, Nib walking Mok at knifepoint, Yerin carrying Jaeha.
Behind them, the gate snaps shut.
The crowd lowers their phones and stares. Then someone starts to clap.
And the whole spillway erupts.
Lyra drops her hunter and steps into the applause, bow high, braid flying. The promised fame has arrived, and she takes the credit.
Nib, who held off seven men, watches her with a flat stare.
Choi shoulders through with four police officers, furious and relieved. He made that call the moment the door shut.
Jaeha sits down hard on the wet concrete. Alive is a generous word.
As the police reach him, Mok finds his arrogance again and plays the wronged guild leader for the cameras.
Then he leans down, low and smug. Who would take a trap-tester's word over his? Nobody ever has.
Jaeha keeps his polite smile. His eyes slide toward Borro.
Out of the moss, the little white drone lifts off, red light on.
The colour leaves Mok's face.
Bomi catches her drone and kisses it, then shows Mok her screen. It was never his word against Jaeha's. It was against a camera.
On her screen, a replay: Mok himself, slashing at Nib.
Black Hound's lawyer from the hearing fights through the crowd, frantically waving Mok quiet.
Mok's jaw clenches. Sweat runs down his temple.
He forces a laugh. A brawl in a gate is one thing, he insists. Gate 0912 is still his story.
Jaeha gets up on Yerin's arm, small and bandaged, and bows like a trap-tester with a question about the route.
Mok looks down his nose. He has never once taken the trap rat's questions seriously.
The crowd goes quiet. First question: the red lamp at Gate 0912. Mok's pride answers before his brain does.
In the crowd, Choi's coffee stops halfway to his mouth.
Next, the fake grade. Mok is so eager to dodge the blame that he names who bought it.
Kanghan, the name on every core battery in Seoul. The chat begs Jaeha to keep going.
Then, very softly, the question Yerin has wanted answered since that night. She was locked in too.
And Mok, stung, shouts the guild's oldest rule at a camera with over a million viewers.
Total silence. A reporter's microphone shakes in his hand.
Jaeha nods slowly, his cold private face on. The last question is the one he came for: Minseok.
Mok lunges against the officers, roaring, and gives up the worst thing he could: who gave the orders at the Han River.
Then he hears what he just said.
One point six million people just heard him say it. Kanghan ordered that door sealed.
Mok stammers back to the official report, the one with his own signature. Behind him, his lawyer clutches his head.
Jaeha lifts the orange phone, the thumbs-up sticker facing Mok. Accidents leave nothing to hide.
Mok's lips move, but nothing comes out.
Nib answers for him: a man who does someone's dirty work keeps proof, in case they turn on him.
Bomi flies the drone up to the cracked screen. She was promised this story first. Now everyone gets it.
The battery is almost gone. One chance to watch, and Jaeha decides he won't watch it alone.
His bloody thumb presses play.
Darkness. Heavy breathing. A small light on wet stone and an orange sleeve.
Hundreds of screens show the same dark image. Nobody makes a sound.
Then Oh Minseok turns the camera on himself, sweating, laughing nervously. He's talking to Jaeha, and he suspects how this ends.
He glances into the dark and whispers. Four years ago he already knew: the grade was a lie, and Mok had the exit covered.
Jaeha watches, tears running through the blood on his face.
Minseok smiles that kind, crooked grin. He had already decided who would go through the door first.
Then his face fills the frame, serious now, and he says the words the report left out.
The image freezes and breaks into blocks.
And the screen goes black. The battery is dead.
Nobody at the spillway moves.
Two million watching, and the chat changes its word: not trap rat, but trap-tester. They say Minseok's name too.
A young hunter takes off his cap and holds it to his chest. Then another. Then a whole row.
Mok's legs give way, and he drops to his knees.
Jaeha limps up on Yerin's arm, the taller one for once. Mok dares him to swing in front of everyone.
Jaeha doesn't raise a hand. He won't do to Mok what Mok did to Minseok. That job belongs to the police.
Mok's face crumples, tears in the eyes that were dead.
The officers cuff him and lift him up, cameras flashing all along the line.
At the car door, Mok stops and looks back at Jaeha. It doesn't sound like a threat. It sounds like a warning.
The door shuts on him.
While every camera points at that car, Han Sora slips away up the wooded hill. Nobody watches her go.
On the rooftop in Mangwon, Seoa cries with relief at her laptop, Gomi in her lap. Even the landlady has softened on pets.
In Kanghan Tower, Director Baek watches the stream on a wall of screens, hands folded on his cane.
He touches his cane, and the screens go dark one by one.
Phone at his ear, the core glowing behind him, Baek smiles. Mok's guild is to vanish. Then he asks what else the dead man's phone caught.
